newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil steady to firm, but buying thin.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil steady to firm, but buying thin.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil was steady to firmer on Monday as crude oil futures rose but dealers said fresh transatlantic barrels were likely to weigh on prices.
High sulphur barges loading in January were traded as low as $91 fob ARA in the morning but prices then rose $3 or $4. Barges for delivery in early February were traded as high as $97.
High sulphur cargoes were quiet. A trader with U.S.-origin barrels was heard to have sold to another trader with a commitment into an Irish utility. Prices were not known.

An ARA player holds a large cargo of Venezuelan fuel oil which is expected to arrive in ARA around February 10. Two other traders are heard holding Venezuelan cargoes, and one of these is likely to move into the Med.

Low sulphur cargoes were steady to firmer. An Italian utility player said he had not been in the market, and offer levels were hard to pin down. A trader said he had seen offers at around $116 cif Med.
Offers of low sulphjur fuel were seen out of the U.K. and Scandinavia.
A refiner in Scandinavia sold a low sulphur cargo to an affiliate in Italy on Monday. The cargo is due to arrive late inb February.
